ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. If $AB=15$, what is the sum of the areas of square $ADEC$ and square $BCFG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the area of square $ADEC$ be: $AC^{2}$, and the area of square $BCFG$ be: $BC^{2}$; \\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC$ is a right triangle, \\
That is, in $\text{Rt}\triangle ABC$, $AB^{2}=AC^{2}+BC^{2}$, with $AB=15$, \\
Then $15^{2}=AC^{2}+BC^{2}=225$. \\
Therefore, the combined area of square $ADEC$ and square $BCFG$ is $\boxed{225}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image it can be seen: the base of triangle ABC is AB, point C is located above AB; on the left there is a square ADEC with AC as a side, and on the right there is a square BCFG with BC as a side.
